source_caption:
BlackBerry (2023) is a biographical drama about the rise of Research In Motion and the creation of the BlackBerry smartphone, once the most powerful device in the business world. The film centers on tech genius Mike Lazaridis and his small team as they build a revolutionary product almost by accident.

As the company grows, businessman Jim Balsillie pushes RIM toward aggressive expansion, money, and control. The movie shows how internal conflicts, ego, and pressure from competitors slowly weaken the company’s vision.

In the end, BlackBerry becomes a cautionary story about success moving too fast. It mixes humor and tension while showing how failing to adapt allowed newer tech giants to overtake them.

source_details.synopsis: BlackBerry is a 2023 Canadian biographical comedy-drama film directed by Matt Johnson from a script he wrote with Matthew Miller. It was loosely adapted from Jacquie McNish and Sean Silcoff's book Losing the Signal: The Untold Story Behind the Extraordinary Rise and Spectacular Fall of BlackBerry. The film is a dramatized account of the history of the BlackBerry line of mobile phones created by co-founders Douglas Fregin (played by Johnson) and Mike Lazaridis (Jay Baruchel), and investor Jim Balsillie (Glenn Howerton). The film also stars Rich Sommer, Michael Ironside, Saul Rubinek, and Cary Elwes in supporting roles. BlackBerry premiered in competition at the 73rd Berlin International Film
